name: Bullpen — Part 1
description: What actually runs at the end of Part 1: two Next.js apps (a public landing site and the trading app) on Vercel Hobby, and a single serverless function backing the trading app's price snapshot endpoint, which in turn calls out to an external market-data provider. No split, no queue, no workflow engine yet — see ADR-0002 for why distribution is deferred until it earns its place.

nodes.name: Reader
nodes.description: A blog reader who lands on the public site to learn about Bullpen.

nodes.name: Player
nodes.description: A registered player who opens the trading app to view prices and (in later parts) place paper trades.

nodes.name: Bullpen Landing
nodes.description: The public landing site (apps/landing) that introduces Bullpen to readers of the blog series.

nodes.name: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.description: The trading app (apps/web) where players will view live prices and place paper trades.

nodes.name: Price Snapshot Service
nodes.description: Serverless function backing GET /api/price/[symbol] in apps/web; fetches a point-in-time price for a symbol from the external market-data provider and returns it to the trading app.

nodes.name: Market Data Provider
nodes.description: External market-data API Bullpen calls for live price snapshots. Provider TBD: a Coinbase-based design was ruled out by Coinbase's Terms of Use, which forbid public display of their data (see issue #6); a terms-of-use-compliant provider has not yet been chosen.

relationships.description: Reader browses the public landing site.
Trading app requests a live price snapshot for a symbol.
Price snapshot service calls out to the external market-data provider for the current price.
